title: The Fintech Opportunity for Students and Gen Z

reader_summary.headline: It's back to school season, and as always, the topic of student loans and education funding is top of mind.
reader_summary.overview: It's back to school season, and as always, the topic of student loans and education funding is top of mind. Beyond the policy debates, though, where can technology be specifically useful to help students and young people navigate some of their first big financial decisions? In this episode from October 2020, Amira Yiyawi, the founder and CEO of Moss, a platform that helps students with their banking needs.

key_points.text: In this episode from October 2020, Amira Yiyawi, the founder and CEO of Moss, a platform that helps students with their banking needs.
key_points.evidence_quote: In this episode from October 2020, Amira Yiyawi, the founder and CEO of Moss, a platform that helps students with their banking needs, like getting financial aid for college, joins A16Z general partner Anish Achari, A6&Z partner Seema Amble and host Lauren Murrow to discuss Fintech for Gen Z and Millennials.

key_points.text: They dig into some of the issues around student loans today, the underserved banking needs of this group.
key_points.evidence_quote: They dig into some of the issues around student loans today, the underserved banking needs of this group, and how fintech can help younger consumers get set up for a better financial future.

key_points.text: Millennials and Gen Z have been hard hit by the one-two punch of the 2008 and 2020 financial crises.
key_points.evidence_quote: Millennials and Gen Z have been hard hit by the one-two punch of the 2008 and 2020 financial crises.

thesis: The episode argues that fintech can help students navigate the complex financial landscape by simplifying access to government aid and reducing reliance on predatory lending. It highlights that traditional banks have largely exited the student market due to regulatory changes and short-term orientation, leaving a gap for new platforms to address bureaucratic hurdles and build credit early.
